column6: Prompt injection never throws — a successful attack reads as a normal Response; token caps also truncate with no flag.
@Guide(.anyOf) does not reliably constrain output — out-of-set values parse cleanly and your switch hits default.
.required has no iteration cap; a tool named in instructions but never registered loops forever with no error.
SpotlightSearchTool hands the model identity attributes only — bodies never arrive and it invents them fluently.
EXIF-rotated camera photos load sideways and get fluent wrong answers; summarizeHistory also flattens attachments away.
String-mode refusals return as successful Strings, not errors, and poison the transcript for later turns.
Transcript.Response's assetIDs is required yet undocumented — Apple's own code passes an array of one empty string.
Cross-reference: session lifetime ties into §7.3's warning that Instruments traces store prompts unencrypted.
A successful prompt injection returns a clean Response with plausible text — no error, guardrail case, or trace shows it.
includeSchemaInPrompt:false without a full example still yields well-formed objects — field semantics quietly degrade.
A tool-call-only turn ends the stream after zero partials — spinner UIs waiting on a first partial hang forever.
Instruments traces store every prompt and response unencrypted — a shared .trace file leaks user text verbatim.
Assigning transcript.history mid-response compiles clean; the failure erupts as an error from an unrelated await.
maximumResponseTokens stops output mid-sentence as a valid Response — no throw and no wasTruncated flag exists.
.required keeps calling tools until you throw from a tool or flip the mode dynamically — there is no default exit.
Exhaustive Transcript.Entry switches break compiling on the 27 SDK; 'fixing' with default: silently drops new cases.
Pointer: the entry payload parameter is undocumented — see the assetIDs callout in §2.5.
Version matrix: LanguageModelSession.GenerationError is deprecated in the 27 SDK — the error surface moved.
Contents entry: @Guide(.anyOf) does not constrain generation.
Contents entry: backends that sample on the GPU expose no logits, so guided generation is lost there.
Apple's documented nested @Generable example fails macro expansion in Xcode 27 beta 27A5228h; move the nested type to file scope until fixed.
GenerationID is stable within one response only — it is not a domain key; matching across responses breaks.
AttachmentLabel output is constrained to be a string, not one of your labels — treat lookup misses as expected.
GenerationGuide.count has both Int and ClosedRange overloads — both exercised in compiling Apple sample code.
Which error catch fires depends on the building Xcode — rebuild with 27 and GenerationError arms stop matching.
Python docstrings leak Swift #/…/# regex delimiters — working tests use bare patterns; do not copy the delimiters.
Heading: .anyOf does not constrain generation.
The model emits values outside your .anyOf set; nothing throws, the String parses, and switches fall to default in prod.
Apple's corrective-string fallback has a reported failure: the model loops re-calling with invalid args — cap retries.
Where the .anyOf constraint is lost — schema serialisation, grammar compilation, or matcher — remains unresolved.
Heading: the logits problem — the fastest backend can lose guided generation.
Engines that sample on the GPU never expose per-step logits — guided generation there is impossible, not degraded.
Propagate .emptyTypeChoicesSchema — it catches unloaded .anyOf arrays; Apple's Skills writes try! there, which traps.
Python's contents.value returns None for a missing key where Swift throws — ported code silently reads null.
streamResponse is neither async nor throwing — schema errors surface later, inside the iteration loop, not at the call.
The iOS 27 metadata: overloads drop includeSchemaInPrompt — the knob moved into ContextOptions.
Apple's ResponseStream snippet does not compile — unbalanced braces, a stray try!, and an undefined variable.
Heading: do not stream in the background — backgrounded streams invite rateLimited; Apple says use respond(to:).
Heading: a stream can finish having yielded zero snapshots.
for try await can complete with zero iterations on a tool-call-only turn — first-snapshot spinners hang, unwraps crash.
Tool-only turns are normal in agentic sessions — zero-snapshot streams occur in routine operation; design for them.
The 1044→700 token saving is Apple's demo on unspecified hardware — reuse the shape of the claim, not the numbers.
Schema off, no example: still structurally valid output, just worse — wrong emphasis, empty strings, grammar padding.
LanguageModelSession.Error is in docs and a forum snippet but no shipping sample — keep the arm, distrust its cases.
Python @fm.generable('description') stores the description and never sends it — the model never sees it.
Heading: three Python-side silent failures, led by options= being dropped when generating= is passed.
Python respond(generating:) drops options= on the floor — temperature, sampling, max tokens have no effect; evals lie.
Python stream_response skips the request lock — a stream and respond() can overlap on one session with no error.
Apple verbatim: recordings capture and store all Foundation Models prompts and responses — guard your traces.
Scope note: covers the OCR/barcode watchOS asymmetry and the attachment label image tools silently require.
Contents entry: .required is a while loop and you own the exit.
Contents entry: the tool you named in instructions but never registered.
A turn whose entire output is a tool call streams nothing — streamResponse completes without yielding one partial.
Tool parameters are computed once at session init and never re-read — late-loaded .anyOf data never reaches the schema.
.anyOf on tool arguments is confirmed broken — a three-city constraint got called with 'Beijing'; validate in the tool.
Exhaustive Transcript.Entry/Segment switches from iOS 26 fail to compile on 27 — .reasoning and .attachment are new.
toolCallingMode is the only non-defaulted param in the 4-arg init — omit it and you get the iOS 26 three-arg overload.
Heading: .required is a while loop and you own the exit.
Apple verbatim: with required tool calling the model is in a while loop — providing an exit condition is your job.
Profile body is re-evaluated per request — 7 evaluations across 3 turns measured; read state there, never mutate.
.preserveTranscript can leave a partially generated last entry — transcript repair is on you before continuing.
Heading: the tool you named but never registered.
Instructions naming an unregistered tool loop with no thrown error — WWDC26 session 243 exists to teach the diagnosis.
The tool-calling Instruments template records prompts and responses — treat .trace files as user data; never commit.
Corrective strings for bad .anyOf args can wedge the model re-calling with invalid args — bound retries yourself.
Throwing from onToolCall stops the whole turn's loop — you cannot reject one tool call and keep the conversation.
An unlabelled attachment is invisible to image tools — everything runs, the barcode or OCR just never reads the image.
BarcodeReaderTool lists watchOS, OCRTool does not — gate watchOS OCR paths; cut feature or doc slip is unresolved.
Unrecognised model types default to the JSON tool-call parser — Mistral [TOOL_CALLS] reads as text and no tool runs.
Community-measured: small models emit tool JSON the framework rejects (decodingFailure) — in-tool baton-pass is shaky.
Symbol table: OCRTool has no watchOS row; its Arguments/Output are absent from the captured Vision interface.
Symbol table: Attachment.label(_:) is required for image tool calls and silently no-ops if omitted.
Contents entry: the metadata gap — the Spotlight defect where the model invents document bodies.
Refactor into a file importing only FoundationModels and the break reads like a missing SDK, not a missing import.
spotlight_search never throws on malformed arguments; a code-100 JSON error rides inside the Prompt output, invisible to catch
Heading: the metadata gap — the defect that will burn you.
The tool call succeeds and returns well-formed items with no bodies — the model's answer is fluent, specific, invented.
Skip calling searchableItemsHandler on any path and Spotlight waits forever — no error, no visible timeout, no results.
Your searchableItems delegate can be wired, compiled, and simply never called — verify it fires before building on it.
SpotlightSearchTool is stream and accumulator — built inline in the tools array, no reference exists to read results.
contextSizeExceeded throws but never says what filled the window — tool result payloads are the invisible culprit.
A CustomStage conforms and is accepted, but the 27.0-beta pipeline never routes items through it — measured no-op.
Model availability is not tool availability — every documented check passes while SpotlightSearchTool fails to init.
Symbol table: Attachment.label(_:) is required for tool calls — silently no-ops when omitted.
A vendored Apple article writes Attachment(image:)/label: — both spellings wrong per the SDK symbol page.
The 27.0 SDK declares exactly four Attachment image inits — CGImage, CIImage, CVPixelBuffer, imageURL; no UIImage.
A URL judged by UTType only — renamed .txt, zero-byte, unscoped file — attaches fine; the answer describes nothing.
EXIF orientation 6 without correction sends the image sideways — the model calls a standing person lying down.
A ResponseStream can end with zero partials on tool-call turns — multimodal turns hit this disproportionately.
For any tool expected to read an image, .label(_:) is mandatory — omit it and the tool silently never sees the image.
summarizeHistory condenses everything into one .prompt entry — attachments vanish and later image answers are invented.
The 27 SDK adds .attachment segments — code with a default: clause silently routes image segments to 'unknown, ignore'.
Apple's article writes GenerationOptions(samplingMode:); Apple's code and the Python SDK write sampling: — unresolved.
The attachment label is how the tool knows which image to read — without it the OCR/barcode call quietly reads nothing.
DetectedObject.boundingBox is always top-left; Segment.box flips on macOS — same code, different y per platform.
Two box encodings in one repo — detector emits DETR [cx,cy,w,h], segmenter XYXY; check what your export produces.
The DETR postprocessor suits set-prediction only — with anchor-based YOLO, decode returns [] and you 'detect nothing'.
On Linux the Python SDK buffers whole responses — streaming arrives in one burst — and @Generable is Darwin-gated.
Image support needs the macOS 27 SDK at build time — a wheel built without it permanently lacks Attachment.
Image attachments leak file descriptors — Python calls fail with Bad file descriptor after ~240-250 sequential requests.
Source note: the coffee/generative-game and SpeechAnalyzer samples surface in searches but are stale iOS 26 evidence.
Read-first: most defects here do not throw — string refusals, out-of-band guardrail changes, incomplete catch ladders.
The availability sample is an iOS 26 project — cite it as the 26 baseline only, never as 2026 guidance.
Do not hardcode 4096 — budgeting below the real window over-compacts and quietly degrades answers; read contextSize.
Community measurement: on-device context reports 4K on iOS 26 but 8K on iOS 27 — probe contextSize at runtime.
Three names circulate for the availability-testing menu — trust the docs' spelling over transcripts.
A reactive-only design missing the SystemLanguageModel.Error arm mishandles availability failures silently.
The 26.5 GenerationError cases are the before side of the rename — never cite them as the 27 error surface.
No source change needed — rebuilding with Xcode 27 is what silently flips which error types your catches see.
Availability failures are SystemLanguageModel.Error, not LanguageModelError — ladders on the latter miss them.
Table: in string mode a model-level refusal does not throw — it returns a refusal string as a successful response.
Heading: the refusal that is just a String.
Decision table: a 'Sorry, I can't…' String is a silent string-mode refusal — switch to Generable so it throws.
permissiveContentTransformations does not apply to @Generable — adopting guided output silently drops permissive mode.
maximumResponseTokens truncates mid-sentence without error — the response arrives valid, just cut off.
rollingWindow is a naive suffix(n), not transcript-aware — it cuts between a prompt and its response.
Modifiers apply outside-in — composed in the obvious order, summarizeHistory can never fire.
preserveTranscript can leave a half-generated entry in history — later turns build on the corrupted tail.
Evidence note: every symbol in the degradation function is cited upstream; refusal detection is deliberately defensive.
Refusal-string detection is a heuristic, not an API — Apple documents only the shape of a refusal.
Symptom table: a polite refusal string with no error is a string-mode refusal — use guided generation to make it throw.
